correctness.rationale: In characteristic two, ∂x and ∂y descend through (x²,y²). Any alternating biderivation is determined by F={x,y}, and Jacobi is a multiderivation vanishing on generator triples; hence all F=a+bx+cy+dxy produce Poisson brackets. Every unital associative automorphism has X=ux+vy+sxy, Y=wx+zy+txy with Δ=uz+vw≠0. Its Jacobian is J=Δ+(ut+ws)x+(vt+zs)y and transformed F′=φ(F)/J. Direct expansion uses (bu+cw)(vt+zs)+(bv+cz)(ut+ws)=Δ(bs+ct) to show coefficient d′=d exactly. Classifying a≠0, a=0 but linear term≠0, and a=b=c=0 yields three disjoint orbits for each d over arbitrary k. Burnside/orbit-stabilizer yields finite-q counts. Independently enumerated all F₂ 16 brackets and 24 automorphisms, producing six orbits sizes 1,1,3,3,4,4; an independently implemented GF₄ enumeration found all 256 brackets, 2880 automorphisms, twelve orbits with four each of sizes 1,15,48. Infinite-field theorem rests on exact algebra not finite experiments.

final_claim: For any characteristic-two field k, all Poisson brackets on k[x,y]/(x²,y²) are isomorphic precisely to one of {x,y}=1+dxy, {x,y}=x+dxy, {x,y}=dxy (d∈k), with d and family intrinsic and no overlaps. Over F_q there are 3q classes and each fixed d has orbit sizes (q−1)q², q²−1,1, with exact stabilizer orders.
